transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maria López (SolacePharm Head of ML), Daniel Carter (Solace Infra), Tanya Reed (Regulatory)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 6–8 week POC: open-model shortlist for clinical-document QA and retrieval-augmented generation, multilingual (EN/ES/PT) coverage, privacy/regulatory constraints (on-prem/VPC and KMS), performance targets and bench plan.

Topics discussed:
- success criteria (accuracy on annotated QA set, latency < 300ms p95 for short queries, throughput targets)
- model candidates (smaller LLaMA variants, Mistral, Falcon-family, MPT-type open models)
- tradeoffs (instruction tuning, hallucination risk, domain fine-tuning vs RAG)
- workload sizing (doc sizes, expected qps, context window needs)
- bench plan, metrics, and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the SolacePharm account. Priya, SE, will lead the bench and model bits.
[00:18] Priya: hi all, thanks. we'll try to keep this pragmatic, focus on what you care about: accuracy on your clinical QA, latency, and how we can run a POC that mirrors production.
[00:32] Maria: yeah thanks. high level: our use case is clinical note parsing + question answering for clinicians and drug safety. bilingual — English and Spanish, also some Portuguese in LATAM. privacy is huge, so we may need private deployment or at least VPC + bring-your-own-KMS.
[00:50] Daniel: and from infra, we want predictable latency and ability to throttle; our ops team will need network diagrams and how Redwood's private plane — uh plane/plane? — control plane, sorry, control plane works with our VPC.
[01:06] Tanya: and regulatory: any PII leakage risk, audit logs, retention policies — we need SOC2, ISO stuff and ability to export logs for audits.
[01:18] Jordan: totally. we'll include SOC2 snapshot and retention options. quick question: what are your success criteria for the POC, Maria?
[01:28] Maria: good question. primary is QA accuracy — we have an internal benchmark (50 annotated questions over 100 notes). want F1 > 0.78 on key intents, and hallucination rate under 5% measured via human review. Secondary: support Spanish parity within 10% of English scores. Latency: for short queries we target p95 under 300ms; for long-document retrieval flows end-to-end under 2s. cost is also a gating factor but secondary.
[01:56] Priya: that gives us clear targets. we'll wire up an eval that measures exact-match, F1, and a hallucination flag metric. for Spanish we can run translation baseline to compare versus model multilinguality.
[02:12] Jordan: about models — for an open-model POC we usually shortlist 3 kinds: 1) a medium-sized LLaMA-family variant (6–13B) that's instruction-tuned, 2) a Mistral or Mistral-like dense model in the 7–12B range for throughput, and 3) a larger instruction-tuned Falcon/MPT candidate for quality baseline. any red flags?
[02:34] Maria: curious on hallucination behavior between them. do you recommend RAG (retrieval-augmented) vs fine-tuning? we can't fine-tune much on PHI.
[02:44] Priya: good point. our recommended approach for sensitive domains is RAG + local KB with strong verifier layers, rather than providing model with raw PHI for fine-tuning. fine-tuning on synthetic or de-identified sets is ok, but for initial POC RAG keeps data residency and reduces hallucination surface.
[03:02] Daniel: what's the context window requirement? clinical notes can be 3–5k tokens, sometimes more.
[03:10] Priya: for retrieval flows, we chunk notes into ~1k token shards, embed them, and retrieve top-K then run the model with the retrieved context. that keeps model memory low; but we can also test 32k window models if you want end-to-end long context. there's a cost-latency tradeoff.
[03:28] Maria: for the clinicians we need the model to reference exact sentence location in the note when it answers — cite evidence. is that straightforward?
[03:36] Priya: yes, RAG with passage-level citations plus a final verification pass. we can measure citation precision as part of the POC metrics.
[03:44] Jordan: let's talk throughput: what QPS are we sizing for the POC vs expected production?
[03:50] Maria: for the POC, ~10 qps peak, sustained 2–3 qps. production could be 50–100 qps depending on rollout.
[03:58] Priya: ok we'll run bench targets at 10 qps with bursts to 25 to test autoscaling and cost per token.
[04:06] Jordan: model shortlist specifics — we'll propose: a) LlamaX-13B-instruct (open checkpoint variant) b) Mistral-7B-instr (or Mistral-ish community fork) c) Falcon-40B-instr-lite as a high-quality baseline. each has different latencies and token costs.
[04:28] Maria: Falcon-40 sounds big — how much more accurate in clinical domain?
[04:34] Priya: often better zero-shot and instruction-following, but bigger means slower and more expensive. on domain data, smaller models with prompt engineering + RAG can match accuracy for many intents. depends on intent complexity — for nuanced pharmacovigilance questions, larger may win.
[04:54] Daniel: do you provide quantized variants? we want to reduce GPU memory footprint for Dedicated.
[04:58] Priya: yes, Redwood supports q4/q8 quantization paths and will recommend kernels per hardware. we'll include quantized throughput numbers in the bench template.
[05:08] Tanya: about data residency — if we do Private deployment on-prem, what's the timeline and what parts of the control plane remain with Redwood?
[05:18] Jordan: for Private we ship a customer-managed control plane option; data paths for inference stay in your VPC. onboarding for on-prem can be 6–12 weeks depending on approvals; VPC-hosted private is typically faster, 3–6 weeks. we'll capture that in the plan.
[05:36] Maria: are there customers in pharma doing this? any references?
[05:40] Jordan: yes, a couple of regulated customers have done RAG POCs with private deploys — we'll share redacted case studies.
[05:46] Priya: about bench metrics — we'll capture: latency p50/p95, throughput, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy metrics (EM, F1), hallucination rate, citation precision, and multilingual delta (ES vs EN).
[06:06] Maria: what's the recommended eval set size? we have only 50 annotated questions; is that too small?
[06:12] Priya: 50 is a reasonable start. for statistical confidence we'd aim for 200 eventually, but for initial POC 50 gives directional signal. include high-priority intents first.
[06:22] Jordan: timeline proposal: week 0 - alignment and data share; week 1-2 - bench harness and infra prep; week 3-4 - run models + collect metrics; week 5 - error analysis and a focused 1-week remediation (prompt tuning / RAG tuning); week 6 - handoff and decision. so 6 weeks total.
[06:42] Maria: that's tight but manageable. approval cycles might add a week.
[06:46] Daniel: networking: we need specifics on egress, IP ranges, peering setup if using VPC.
[06:54] Jordan: noted. we'll include a networking checklist and require Daniel's diagram.
[07:00] Priya: model selection notes: we'll test instruction-tuned checkpoints first. candidate list we'll propose: "LlamaX-13B-instruct (6-13B family)"; "Mistral-7B-instr (or close community fork)"; "Falcon-40B-instr-lite (quality baseline)"; optional test: a 32k-window Llama-variant for long-context scenarios.
[07:26] Maria: how do you measure hallucination automatically? is that manual labeling?
[07:30] Priya: a mix — automated hallucination heuristics (answer not supported by retrieved passages) plus a small manual review sample. we surface a hallucination score and examples.
[07:40] Tanya: are there any certifications needed for on-prem? we sometimes need ISO27001.
[07:44] Jordan: we can provide compliance artifact packages; private/on-prem reduces scope, but we'll map what remains in scope.
[07:54] Maria: cost question: how do you present cost. is it per-token + infra?
[07:58] Jordan: for hosted it's per-token + infra amortized. for Dedicated it's a reserved capacity seat model with a monthly commit. we'll give a POC estimate for each shortlist: approx tokens, GPU hours for bench runs, and projected monthly unit cost for production QPS.
[08:18] Daniel: any constraints on embedding store? we prefer self-managed vector DB (we use Milvus). will Redwood integrate?
[08:24] Priya: yes, Redwood supports external vector stores via connectors; for POC we can integrate with Milvus, or use Redwood-managed store for speed. we'll include both options and cost deltas.
[08:38] Maria: for Spanish, do you have any model recommendations that are known to be stronger?
[08:44] Priya: Mistral and some LLaMA forks show decent multilingual performance; plus a translation-backstop approach: translate to English, run the model, then translate back, that's a baseline to compare. native multilingual models reduce translation artifacts.
[08:58] Jordan: on benchmarks we'll compare native ES performance vs translated pipeline as a separate axis.
[09:04] Maria: okay. sample data — we'll strip PHI and provide de-identified notes. can we also test with a synthetic PHI set to simulate edge cases?
[09:12] Priya: yes synthetic is helpful. we also recommend a small adversarial set with tricky prompts to stress hallucination.
[09:20] Jordan: next steps recap: Jordan sends security pack + bench template; Priya shares model shortlist + harness repo; Solace shares redacted notes and 50 annotated QA; schedule infra deep-dive with Daniel.
[09:34] Maria: sounds good. one more: can the POC include a simple UI mock for clinician flows? seeing latency and citations in a UI helps decision makers.
[09:44] Jordan: yes we can spin up a basic front-end for demo — we'll estimate dev time in the next email.
[09:50] Tanya: also retention — how long are logs kept during POC? we need to ensure patient data is not retained beyond agreement.
[09:58] Jordan: retention will be configurable; for POC we recommend short retention and automatic purge options. we'll reflect that in the security doc.
[10:08] Priya: operational knobs we'll test: batching sizes, cache TTL for embeddings, prefix KV cache for conversational flows, and quantization profiles. we'll capture the knobs and expected latency/cost impacts.
[10:26] Daniel: when you say 300ms p95, is that cold-start included?
[10:30] Priya: we'll measure steady-state; we'll also capture cold-start for scale-up events. cold-start can add 1–2s depending on model size and GPU pool.
[10:40] Maria: for the POC who signs what? do we need an MSA?
[10:44] Jordan: for POC we usually do a short statement-of-work (SOW) and an addendum on data handling. we'll send a POC SOW template.
[10:52] Maria: ok. any blockers from Redwood side?
[10:56] Jordan: no blockers. main dependency is your data and network info. Priya will need the annotated set and the infra diagram.
[11:04] Maria: we'll aim to get those by next week.
[11:08] Priya: I'll also include suggested prompt templates and a small set of instruction-tuning examples (not PHI) to show how prompt engineering helps.
[11:18] Jordan: competitor note — we sometimes get asked about Anthropic for safety and OpenAI for quality; we discussed where open models land in between and how RAG + safety layers can close the gap.
[11:30] Tanya: thanks, that's helpful.
[11:34] Jordan: wrapping up: Jordan will email the pack, Priya will post the repo link, Maria to share docs, Daniel to share network diagram, Tanya to confirm compliance checklist items. Any last questions?
[11:46] Maria: none. thanks everyone.
[11:50] Jordan: thanks all, we’ll follow up with dates.

End of meeting.
